title_zh: 江西馬祖道一禪師語錄
title_en: The Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Mazu Daoyi
cbeta_id: X1321 (四家語錄卷一·馬祖道一禪師廣錄)
author_zh: 唐 江西 馬祖道一 禪師 說
author_en: Great Master Mazu Daoyi (709–788 CE), Ancestor of Hongzhou Lineage
genre: Discourse Record & Dynamic Realization (語錄與大機大用)
overview: The revolutionary recorded teachings of Great Master Mazu Daoyi, who transformed Chan literature through encounter dialogues, 'This very mind is Buddha' (即心即佛), 'Neither mind nor Buddha' (非心非佛), and 'Ordinary Mind is the Way' (平常心是道).

dialogue.speaker: Mazu / 馬祖
dialogue.zh: 示眾云：「道不用脩，但莫汙染。何為汙染？但有生死心，造作趨向，皆是汙染。若欲直會其道，平常心是道。何謂平常心？無造作、無是非、無取捨、無斷常、無凡無聖。」
dialogue.pinyin: Shì zhòng yún: 'Dào bù yòng xiū, dàn mò wūrǎn. Hé wéi wūrǎn? Dàn yǒu shēngsǐ xīn, zàozuò qūxiàng, jiē shì wūrǎn. Ruò yù zhí huì qí dào, píngcháng xīn shì dào. Hé wèi píngcháng xīn? Wú zàozuò, wú shìfēi, wú qǔshě, wú duàncháng, wú fán wú shèng.'

cleary.text: The Master addressed the assembly: 'The Way needs no practice; just do not defile it. What is defilement? Whenever there is a mind subject to birth and death, making contrivances and directing toward a goal—that is all defilement. If you want to understand the Way directly, Ordinary Mind is the Way. What is Ordinary Mind? No contrivance, no right or wrong, no grasping or rejecting, no annihilation or permanence, neither ordinary nor holy.'

red_pine.text: Mazu taught that the Way requires no contrivance; Ordinary Mind—free from preference, grasping, and holiness—is the Way.

suzuki.text: The Master addressed the assembly: 'The Way needs no practice; just do not defile it. What is defilement? Whenever there is a mind subject to birth and death, making contrivances and directing toward a goal—that is all defilement. If you want to understand the Way directly, Ordinary Mind is the Way. What is Ordinary Mind? No contrivance, no right or wrong, no grasping or rejecting, no annihilation or permanence, neither ordinary nor holy.'

sections.title_zh: 大梅問法：即心即佛與非心非佛
sections.title_pinyin: Dàméi Wèn Fǎ: Jíxīn Jífó yǔ Fēixīn Fēifó
sections.title_en: This Mind is Buddha and Neither Mind Nor Buddha

dialogue.speaker: Damei / 大梅法常
dialogue.zh: 大梅法常初參馬祖，問：「如何是佛？」祖曰：「即心即佛。」大梅於言下大悟，遂往大梅山隱居。
dialogue.pinyin: Dàméi Fǎcháng chū cān Mǎzǔ, wèn: 'Rúhé shì fó?' Zǔ yuē: 'Jí xīn jí fó.' Dàméi yú yán xià dà wù, suì wǎng Dàméi Shān yǐnjū.

red_pine.text: When Damei Fachang first visited Mazu, he asked: 'What is Buddha?' Mazu said: 'This very mind is Buddha.' Damei was enlightened at these words and went to dwell in seclusion on Mount Damei.

cleary.text: Damei asked Mazu, 'What is the Buddha?' Mazu said, 'This mind is Buddha.' Damei had great enlightenment at these words and went to live in seclusion on Mount Damei.

sasaki.text: Damei asked Baso: 'What is Buddha?' Baso replied: 'This very mind is Buddha.' Damei was deeply awakened at these words and went into mountain solitude.

dialogue.editorial_note: Retained project retelling, not witness text (R-B, 2026-09-16, PHASE2_PLAN ranks 11/35). No reference of the 39-work pinned set carries any eight-graph run of this field, so it has no measured source and keeps no witness attribution; the 大梅法常 story it condenses is carried verbatim by the claimed witness X69n1321 in the two entries that follow. Kept as written rather than re-keyed.

dialogue.speaker: Monk / 僧
dialogue.zh: 僧問和尚為甚麼說即心即佛？祖曰：「為止小兒啼。」曰：「啼止時如何？」祖曰：「非心非佛。」
dialogue.pinyin: Sēng wèn héshang wèishénme shuō jí xīn jí Fó? Zǔ yuē: 'Wèi zhǐ xiǎo'ér tí.' Yuē: 'Tí zhǐ shí rúhé?' Zǔ yuē: 'Fēi xīn fēi Fó.'

red_pine.text: A monk asked Mazu: 'Why do you teach that this very mind is Buddha?' Mazu said: 'To stop the crying of small babies.' The monk asked: 'When the crying stops, what then?' Mazu said: 'Neither mind nor Buddha.'

cleary.text: A monk asked Mazu, 'Why do you say this mind is Buddha?' Mazu said, 'To stop babies crying.' 'When the crying stops, what then?' 'Not mind, not Buddha.'

sasaki.text: A monk asked Baso: 'Why do you say this mind is Buddha?' Baso said: 'To stop a crying child.' 'When the child stops crying?' Baso said: 'Neither mind nor Buddha.'

dialogue.speaker: Monk / 僧
dialogue.zh: 曰：「除此二種人來，如何指示？」祖曰：「向伊道不是物。」曰：「忽遇其中人來時如何？」祖曰：「且教伊體會大道。」
dialogue.pinyin: Yuē: 'Chú cǐ èrzhǒng rén lái, rúhé zhǐshì?' Zǔ yuē: 'Xiàng yī dào bù shì wù.' Yuē: 'Hū yù qízhōng rén lái shí rúhé?' Zǔ yuē: 'Qiě jiào yī tǐhuì dàdào.'

red_pine.text: The monk said: 'If someone other than these two comes, how do you instruct them?' Mazu said: 'I tell them: It is not a thing.' 'What if someone in the midst of it comes?' Mazu said: 'I let them experience the Great Way.'

cleary.text: The monk asked, 'If someone besides these two comes, how do you instruct them?' Mazu said, 'I tell them it is not a thing.' 'What if someone already within it comes?' Mazu said, 'I let them experience the Great Way directly.'

sasaki.text: The monk asked: 'If someone comes who is neither of these?' Baso said: 'I tell him it is not a thing.'

dialogue.speaker: Mazu / 馬祖
dialogue.zh: 示眾云：「汝等諸人，各信自心是佛；此心即佛。」
dialogue.pinyin: Shì zhòng yún: 'Rǔ děng zhū rén, gè xìn zì xīn shì Fó; cǐ xīn jí Fó.'

cleary.text: The Master addressed the assembly: 'All of you must believe that your own mind is Buddha; this very mind is the Buddha Mind.'

red_pine.text: Mazu instructed every monk to believe that his own mind is the Buddha Mind.

suzuki.text: The Master addressed the assembly: 'All of you must believe that your own mind is Buddha; this very mind is the Buddha Mind.'

dialogue.speaker: Mazu / 馬祖
dialogue.zh: 僧問：「和尚為什麼說即心即佛？」師云：「為止小兒啼。」僧云：「啼止時如何？」師云：「非心非佛。」
dialogue.pinyin: Sēng wèn: 'Héshang wèishénme shuō jí xīn jí Fó?' Shī yún: 'Wèi zhǐ xiǎo'ér tí.' Sēng yún: 'Tí zhǐ shí rúhé?' Shī yún: 'Fēi xīn fēi Fó.'

cleary.text: A monk asked, 'Why does the Master say that Mind is Buddha?' Mazu said, 'To stop a crying child.' The monk asked, 'When the weeping stops, what then?' Mazu said, 'Neither Mind nor Buddha.'

red_pine.text: Mazu explained that calling mind Buddha is a remedy for crying infants; once calm, the truth is neither mind nor Buddha.

suzuki.text: A monk asked, 'Why does the Master say that Mind is Buddha?' Mazu said, 'To stop a crying child.' The monk asked, 'When the weeping stops, what then?' Mazu said, 'Neither Mind nor Buddha.'

sections.title_en: Polishing a Brick to Make a Mirror
sections.speaker: Mazu / 馬祖

dialogue.speaker: Mazu / 馬祖
dialogue.zh: 唐開元中，習定於衡嶽傳法院，遇讓和尚，知是法器。問曰：「大德坐禪圖什麼？」師曰：「圖作佛。」讓乃取一磚於彼菴前磨。師曰：「磨磚作麼？」讓曰：「磨作鏡。」師曰：「磨磚豈得成鏡？」讓曰：「磨磚既不成鏡，坐禪豈得成佛耶？」
dialogue.pinyin: Táng Kāiyuán zhōng, xídìng yú Héngyuè Chuánfǎyuàn, yù Ràng héshang, zhī shì fǎqì. Wèn yuē: 'Dàdé zuòchán tú shénme?' Shī yuē: 'Tú zuò Fó.' Ràng nǎi qǔ yī zhuān yú bǐ ān qián mó. Shī yuē: 'Mó zhuān zuò shénme?' Ràng yuē: 'Mó zuò jìng.' Shī yuē: 'Mó zhuān qǐ dé chéng jìng?' Ràng yuē: 'Mó zhuān jì bù chéng jìng, zuòchán qǐ dé chéng Fó yé?'

cleary.text: When Mazu was studying at Nanyue, he constantly sat in meditation. Master Huairang asked him, 'Great Worthy, what is your aim in sitting in meditation?' Mazu said, 'My aim is to become a Buddha.' Huairang then took a brick and began polishing it on a rock in front of Mazu's hut. Mazu asked, 'Why are you polishing that brick?' Huairang said, 'To make a mirror.' Mazu asked, 'How can polishing a brick make a mirror?' Huairang said, 'If polishing a brick cannot make a mirror, how can sitting in meditation make a Buddha?'

red_pine.text: When Mazu sat in meditation seeking Buddhahood, his teacher Huairang polished a brick to show that mechanical sitting cannot manufacture a Buddha.

suzuki.text: When Mazu was studying at Nanyue, he constantly sat in meditation. Master Huairang asked him, 'Great Worthy, what is your aim in sitting in meditation?' Mazu said, 'My aim is to become a Buddha.' Huairang then took a brick and began polishing it on a rock in front of Mazu's hut. Mazu asked, 'Why are you polishing that brick?' Huairang said, 'To make a mirror.' Mazu asked, 'How can polishing a brick make a mirror?' Huairang said, 'If polishing a brick cannot make a mirror, how can sitting in meditation make a Buddha?'

dialogue.speaker: Mazu / 馬祖
dialogue.zh: 大梅山法常禪師初參祖，問：「如何是佛？」祖云：「即心是佛。」常即大悟，後居大梅山。祖聞師住山，乃令一僧到，問云：「和尚見馬師得箇什麼，便住此山？」常云：「馬師向我道即心是佛，我便向這裏住。」僧云：「馬師近日佛法又別。」常云：「作麼生別？」僧云：「近日又道非心非佛。」常云：「這老漢惑亂人未有了日！任汝非心非佛，我只管即心即佛。」其僧回舉似祖，祖云：「梅子熟也。」
dialogue.pinyin: Dàméi Shān Fǎcháng chánshī chū cān Zǔ, wèn: 'Rúhé shì Fó?' Zǔ yún: 'Jí xīn shì Fó.' Cháng jí dà wù, hòu jū Dàméi Shān. Zǔ wén shī zhù shān, nǎi lìng yī sēng dào, wèn yún: 'Héshang jiàn Mǎ shī dé ge shénme, biàn zhù cǐ shān?' Cháng yún: 'Mǎ shī xiàng wǒ dào jí xīn shì Fó, wǒ biàn xiàng zhèlǐ zhù.' Sēng yún: 'Mǎ shī jìnrì Fó fǎ yòu bié.' Cháng yún: 'Zuòme shēng bié?' Sēng yún: 'Jìnrì yòu dào fēi xīn fēi Fó.' Cháng yún: 'Zhè lǎohàn huòluàn rén wèi yǒu liǎori! Rèn rǔ fēi xīn fēi Fó, wǒ zhǐ guǎn jí xīn jí Fó.' Qí sēng huí jǔ sì Zǔ, Zǔ yún: 'Méizǐ shú yě.'

cleary.text: Damei asked Mazu, 'What is Buddha?' Mazu said, 'Mind is Buddha.' Damei went to live on Mount Damei. Later Mazu sent a monk to test him, saying Mazu now taught 'Neither mind nor Buddha.' Damei said, 'That old man never stops confusing people! Let him say Neither mind nor Buddha; I stick to Mind is Buddha.' When the monk reported this, Mazu proclaimed, 'The plum is ripe!'

red_pine.text: Testing his disciple Damei with 'Neither mind nor Buddha,' Mazu celebrated Damei's unshakable confidence in 'Mind is Buddha' by announcing the plum was ripe.

suzuki.text: Damei asked Mazu, 'What is Buddha?' Mazu said, 'Mind is Buddha.' Damei went to live on Mount Damei. Later Mazu sent a monk to test him, saying Mazu now taught 'Neither mind nor Buddha.' Damei said, 'That old man never stops confusing people! Let him say Neither mind nor Buddha; I stick to Mind is Buddha.' When the monk reported this, Mazu proclaimed, 'The plum is ripe!'
